en: A past state is not a condition for a present state by way of the root-condition.
A future state is not a condition for a present state by way of the root-condition. Past and future states together are not conditions for a present state by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root-condition (hetu), three; with respect to object (ārammaṇa) and predominance (adhipati), seven; with respect to proximity (anantara), three ... pe ... with respect to support (nissaya), three; with respect to decisive support (upanissaya), seven; with respect to prenascence (purejāta) and postnascence (pacchājāta), three ...
pe ... with respect to non-disappearance (avigata), three. Dependent on a state whose object is not past, a state whose object is past arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state whose object is not past, a state whose object is future arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state whose object is not past ... [and so forth].
Dependent on [a state] having a present object, a state with a present object arises by way of root condition … three.

Dependent on a state not having a future object, a state with a past object arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state not having a future object, a state with a present object arises by way of root condition … two.
Dependent on a state not having a present object, a state with a present object arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state with a non-present object, a state with a past object arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state with a non-present object, a state with a future object arises by way of root condition ...

With respect to cause, there are seventeen; with respect to object, fifteen; with respect to predominance, nine ... pe ... with respect to prenascence and repetition, nine ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance, seventeen.
